children: , the social-media and AI platform, rejected calls for a coordinated slowdown in advanced AI development, Reuters reported Wednesday. The shares gained approximately 1.5% to $680.41, keeping the stock firmly in positive territory even as investors weighed the increasingly difficult trade-off between AI speed and AI safety.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg argued that competitive pressure and legal liability already push individual AI laboratories to take safety seriously. He pointed to Meta's decision to delay Muse for further security work and said independent model evaluations should become a normal part of the industry. Zuckerberg also noted that most of Meta's computing power remains focused on existing products rather than systems designed to improve themselves, drawing a line between today's commercial AI race and more advanced autonomous models.

That distinction matters because Meta is spending at extraordinary scale. The company invested $31.08 billion in second-quarter capital expenditures, equal to roughly 51.1% of revenue, while free cash flow fell to just $784 million. The valuation picture offers some cushion: the chart shows Meta trading at $680.41 versus a GF Value of $853.42, or about 20.27% below that estimate. Investors are therefore being asked to balance a sizeable valuation discount against the execution risk of pouring tens of billions of dollars into an AI race where one major safety failure could damage both user trust and the returns expected from that infrastructure.

title: Meta Rises as Zuckerberg Rejects an Industrywide AI Brake
